previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent cellulitis, and venous stasis ulcers was admitted for worsening left leg cellulitis around non-healing ulcers. She presented with erythema, swelling, and yellow drainage, having failed outpatient antibiotic therapy. She was treated with IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin initially, then transitioned to oral doxycycline after developing hives to Bactrim. Imaging showed no evidence of osteomyelitis or deep vein thrombosis. The vascular surgery team recommended compression, elevation, and wound care. She improved clinically and was discharged home with home health services, a 10-day course of doxycycline, and follow-up plans for wound care and colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia.
